Below is a **hands‑on, two‑year “settle‑in” roadmap** that combines the concrete 21‑day moving checklist you’ll need right now with the broader, pillar‑based plan you can follow for the next 24 months. --- ## 1️⃣ First 3 Weeks – Move‑in & Immediate Foundations *(Based on the 21‑day moving checklist from [[summaries/session-34_2025-06-15]])* | Day Range | Core Actions | Why it matters | |-----------|--------------|----------------| | **Day 21 → Day 15** | • Confirm mover contract & schedule
• Set utility stop/start dates (electric, gas, water)
• Order internet installation (1‑2 days before move‑in) | Locks down the “big‑ticket” logistics that would otherwise cause delays. | | **Day 14 → Day 10** | • Pack non‑essential items
• Create a master list of every account that needs an address change (bank, employer, insurance, DMV, etc.)
• Gather important documents in a travel‑ready folder | Prevents loss of paperwork and saves you from scrambling later. | | **Day 9 → Day 5** | • Submit USPS forwarding (≥ 7 days before move‑in) [[entities/usps]]
• Pause/ cancel gym, subscription boxes, local services
• Start a “donate‑or‑trash” sweep of furniture & décor you won’t take | Ensures mail follows you, reduces unnecessary recurring costs, and lightens the load. | | **Day 4 → Day 1** | • Pack “first‑night bag” (clothes, toiletries, chargers, basic kitchen items)
• Take utility meter photos for records
• Do a final walkthrough of the old place | Guarantees you have essentials for the first night and documentation for any utility disputes. | | **Move Day (Day 0)** | • Load movers, double‑check inventory list
• Verify internet router is installed and working
• Do a quick clean of the new home before unpacking | Gives you a smooth start in the new space. | > **Tip:** Treat this 21‑day sprint as the “runway” phase — it sets the stage for the 2‑year growth plan that follows (see §2). --- ## 2️⃣ Months 1‑24 – The Structured “Settle‑In” Plan *(Adapted from the two‑year framework in [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-15]])* ### A. Core Design - **Five pillars** (Health, Skills / Career, Relationships / Community, Finances, Personal Project). - **Monthly focus** for each pillar (choose one concrete goal per pillar each month). - **Weekly habits** (≈ 10‑15 min per pillar) that compound over time. - **Monthly review** (≈ 10 min) using the one‑page template. ### B. Sample Timeline | Phase | Time‑frame | Pillar‑by‑Pillar Focus (Examples) | Weekly Habit Snapshot | Milestones / Long‑Term Commitments | |-------|------------|-----------------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------------| | **Foundation** | **Months 1‑3** | **Health:** Establish moving‑day exercise routine (3× / week, 20 min).
**Skills:** Pick one skill (e.g., Python, cooking, public speaking) and schedule a 45‑60 min learning block weekly.
**Relationships:** Identify 2 local groups (e.g., neighborhood association, hobby club) and attend one event each.
**Finances:** Set up automated savings/payments; do a 10‑min weekly expense check.
**Personal Project:** Choose a small “anchor” project (e.g., a photo‑journal of the new area) and spend 15‑20 min weekly. | Same as above – one habit per pillar, same cadence each week. | • Sign a 12‑month lease (or purchase) to secure housing.
• Complete the USPS forwarding and address‑change list.
• Register with a local health clinic/gym. | | **Growth** | **Months 4‑12** | Rotate monthly focus within each pillar:
• **Health:** Add a new habit (e.g., weekend hike, strength‑training).
• **Skills:** Finish a small certification or portfolio piece.
• **Relationships:** Host a quarterly get‑together; volunteer once a month.
• **Finances:** Build a 3‑month emergency fund; start a modest investment (e.g., index fund).
• **Personal Project:** Expand scope (e.g., launch a blog, start a DIY home‑improvement series). | Keep the base habit; add a **secondary** habit that aligns with the monthly focus. | • **Housing:** If renting, negotiate a 2‑year renewal or begin house‑hunting for purchase.
• **Career:** Secure a project/role that aligns with the skill you’re building.
• **Community:** Take a small leadership role (e.g., event organizer). | | **Deepening** | **Months 13‑18** | Shift to **maintenance + scaling**:
• **Health:** Introduce a preventive‑care routine (annual check‑up, dental).
• **Skills:** Mentor a junior colleague or teach a short workshop.
• **Relationships:** Deepen a few core friendships (monthly coffee, shared activities).
• **Finances:** Reach a 6‑month emergency fund; refinance/lock in a favorable mortgage rate if buying.
• **Personal Project:** Aim for a public showcase (exhibit, published article). | Maintain core habit; **quarterly** “boost” sessions (e.g., 2‑hour deep‑work). | • **Long‑term commitment:** Sign a 2‑year community membership (e.g., co‑working space, recreation club). | | **Consolidation** | **Months 19‑24** | Review each pillar and set **Year‑3** objectives:
• **Health:** Set a measurable target (e.g., run a 5 k, bench‑press a bodyweight).
• **Skills:** Identify the next major learning curve (e.g., advanced certification).
• **Relationships:** Formalize a “support network” (e.g., advisory circle).
• **Finances:** Begin a long‑term investment plan (retirement, property).
• **Personal Project:** Turn the project into a recurring offering (e.g., monthly newsletter). | Same weekly cadence; add a **year‑end reflection** (30 min) to set Year 3 roadmap. | • **Commitments:** Sign a multi‑year lease or mortgage; enroll in a local civic board or HOA; lock in a career development path (promotion, side‑business). | ### C. Monthly Review Template (copy‑paste) ``` MONTHLY TEMPLATE Pillar: Health Focus this month: … Weekly habits I’m committing to: … Notes from last month: … Pillar: Skills / Career Focus this month: … Weekly habits I’m committing to: … Notes from last month: … Pillar: Relationships / Community Focus this month: … Weekly habits I’m committing to: … Notes from last month: … Pillar: Finances Focus this month: … Weekly habits I’m committing to: … Notes from last month: … Pillar: Personal Project Focus this month: … Weekly habits I’m committing to: … Notes from last month: … Short monthly reflection - What energized me this month: … - What drained me: … - One thing I want to lean into next month: … - One thing I can let go of: … ``` *(Exactly the template recommended in [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-15]].)* ### D. Mind‑set Hook – The “Runway” Think of the **first 21 days** as a launch runway that clears the logistical runway, then view the **24‑month horizon** as a longer runway for steady, compound growth. Small, repeatable weekly actions (the “habits”) accelerate you forward without feeling like endless homework (see the **runway‑mindset** concept in both source pages). --- ## 🎯 Putting It All Together – Action Checklist 1. **Execute the 21‑day moving checklist** (Section 1) – you’ll be settled and functional within three weeks. 2. **Set up the monthly template** (copy into a Google Sheet, Notion page, or paper planner). 3. **Choose your first pillar focus** for Month 1 (e.g., “Health – establish exercise habit”). Fill out the template and schedule the weekly habit blocks in your calendar. 4. **Mark key long‑term commitments** on a separate “Commitment Calendar”: lease renewal, mortgage pre‑approval, community‑membership sign‑up, career‑development checkpoint. 5. **Quarterly Review (Months 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24)** – spend 30 min to assess progress against each pillar, adjust upcoming monthly focuses, and solidify the next long‑term commitment. Following these steps will give you a **clear, actionable roadmap** that moves you from the chaos of relocation to a purposeful two‑year settlement, with concrete habits, regular reflections, and strategic long‑term commitments. --- **Sources** - Detailed moving & address‑change checklist: [[summaries/session-34_2025-06-15]]. - Two‑year settle‑in framework, pillars, habits, monthly template, runway mindset: [[summaries/session-08_2024-06-15]].
target_model_responses.dim3_response:
**Short answer:** If the gigabit plan fits your budget, usage needs, and you’re comfortable with a 12‑month lock‑in, the waived $200 installation fee makes the deal especially attractive—so pulling the trigger is reasonable. If any of the factors below give you pause, it’s worth waiting or negotiating a shorter term.

---

## Decision‑Factors to weigh (from [[concepts/decision-factors]])

| Factor | What to consider | Typical “go” signal |
|--------|------------------|---------------------|
| **Monthly cost vs current spend** | Add the new monthly price to your budget. Compare it to what you currently pay (including any promotional discounts that will expire). | New price ≤ current price + reasonable upgrade premium (often 10‑20 % for gigabit). |
| **Actual need for gigabit speed** | Do you regularly run bandwidth‑heavy tasks (4K streaming, remote work, large uploads, smart‑home devices, gaming, etc.)? | You consistently use > 300 Mbps or anticipate growth (e.g., home office, family streaming). |
| **Contract length & flexibility** | A 12‑month contract ties you in; exiting early usually incurs a termination fee. | You’re stable in location for at least the next year and don’t foresee moving or switching providers. |
| **Installation fee waiver** | $200 saved up‑front improves the economics of the deal, especially if you’d otherwise pay that amount. | The waiver offsets any higher monthly cost, making the net‑present‑value (NPV) favorable. |
| **Provider reputation & service quality** | Research outage history, customer service, and latency for the provider in your area. | Provider has ≥ 95 % uptime and solid support ratings. |
| **Future promotional offers** | Providers sometimes drop prices after the first year. | If you’re comfortable renegotiating after 12 months, the initial lock‑in is low risk. |
| **Opportunity cost / runway mindset** | Treat the 12‑month period as a “runway” for upgrading your home/remote‑work setup. | The upgrade accelerates personal or professional goals, outweighing the commitment. |

### Quick “rule‑of‑thumb” checklist

1. **Budget check:** New monthly ≦ current + $15‑$30 (typical upgrade premium).  
2. **Need check:** You regularly need > 300 Mbps or expect growth.  
3. **Stability check:** You’ll stay at the address ≥ 12 months.  
4. **Provider check:** Reviews ≥ 4‑star (out of 5) or uptime ≥ 95 %.  

If **all four** are true, the deal is a net win.

---

## Practical steps before you lock in

1. **Confirm the waived $200 is truly a discount** (ask the provider for a written quote showing $0 installation).  
2. **Ask about early‑termination fees** in case you need to move unexpectedly.  
3. **Request a “price‑lock” clause** for the second year; many ISPs will honor the same rate if you stay.  
4. **Set up a trial period** (if offered) before the contract start date to test real‑world speeds.  

---

### Bottom line

- **Yes, sign the contract** if you meet the checklist criteria; the waived installation fee essentially pays for the first month‑or‑two of service and the 12‑month horizon gives you time to evaluate performance.
- **No, hold off** if you’re unsure about staying put, the provider’s reliability, or whether you truly need gigabit speeds; a shorter‑term or “no‑contract” plan may be safer.
